rows.why: He described خطيبتي (feminine) with masculine عيان; Amal recast عيانة and he repeated 'عيانة' at 02:26.
Amal recast the order to topic + body part + verb (هي راسها بيوجع) and he repeated it at 04:07.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: He said he did not know 'cough'; Amal supplied كحة - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: الـ or لا الـ نار. / لـ النار for fire
rows.amal_said: Men not. You're worried from. ... Men، men.
rows.why: With قلقانين he used لـ for 'about'; Amal said 'You're worried from... Men' and he said من نار - قلقان takes من.

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.why: For 'a fire will start' he tried يبدأ; Amal said no, another word is used (she did not give it).

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: He asked how to say 'taking care'; Amal supplied ديرت بالي.
دير بال takes على; he joined خطيبتي straight onto بال and Amal recast بالي على خطيبتي.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.why: Two minutes after her fix he again left out على; Amal named it ('بدير بالي takes على') and he said ديرت بالي على خطيبتي - a second voiced fix of the same slip.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: For the 'take care' command he said ديري باليك; Amal gave the command دير بالك (no -ي on بال).
After خلينا the verb is a bare present; he used past عملنا and Amal recast نعمل, which he repeated.

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه إنتي... / الدرس إنه، إنه تخطط-- تفتتلي.
rows.why: 'The lesson that you planned' needs اللي, not إنه; Amal only asked 'كيف يعني؟' (did not understand) and did not fix it. Right form is my reading.
تفتتلي is not a word for 'you planned'; he started تخطط (right root) then switched to a non-word; Amal's 'كيف يعني' shows she did not understand.
Asked what is in the sky he said غيم; Amal asked 'just one?' and he changed to the plural غيوم.

rows.medi_said: Uh, عصا- is it، أسف؟ ... is it عصافير؟ ... أنا نسيته.
rows.why: He could not find 'sky' (tried عصافير, which Amal said is birds) and said أنا نسيته; Amal supplied سما.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.why: Listening: he heard her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you watch the sky'; Amal said no, that would be بتتطلع - بتطلع here is 'rises'.

rows.medi_said: أنا نسيت الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.why: He produced سجر for dawn (not a word); Amal gave فجر and he asked 'Is it فجر or سجر?' then took فجر.
For 'other than' he said غير لو; Amal said 'No لو. غير.' - the extra لو is wrong (she later says لو goes with حتى لو).
The known sky needs el- (السما); Amal recast السما بالليل and he repeated it.
Asked 'it's dark at night', he said he forgot; Amal supplied عتمة.
'One' goes after the noun (شمس واحدة); Amal only echoed واحدة and praised the gender, so the order was let pass. Right form is my reading.
After the feminine نجمة, تاني must be تانية; Amal echoed تاني as a prompt and he changed to تانية, which she accepted.
With the object fronted the verb needs a pointer; Amal named it and he fixed to بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer rule').
rows.english: This is the first star I see today.

rows.medi_said: since is لسـ-- لسا, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He asked for 'since', guessing لسا then لا; Amal said no and supplied من.
For 'it rained' he could not land the past form; Amal gave مطرت and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: So the air would be الأول هون.
rows.why: He said الأول (the first) for 'the air'; Amal recast الهوا and, when he asked what he said, told him الأول.

rows.medi_said: آآ، بعيد من cuz it's comparative, right?
rows.why: For 'different than' he used من; Amal said عن and his final line is الهواء هون غير عن الهواء هناك. Engine wrote بعيد / بيد - likely غير misheard (his final sentence uses غير).
rows.english: The air here is different from the air there.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... صح. آخر مرة. The last time.
rows.why: آخر + el- means 'the end of'; for 'the last time' it is آخر مرة, which Amal explained and he took.
The subject مرة is feminine; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he fixed to كانت.
rows.english: The last time was three years ago.

rows.why: سنان means teeth (Amal asked 'What's سنان?' - 'teeth'); 'years' is سنين.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين ... would be for the last three years. ... Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: For 'ago' he used الماضي; Amal said no (that means 'the last three years') and gave قبل.
Amal recast the past form تَلَّجَت and he repeated it; may be only vowel length (pronunciation) - he had said تلجت right at 35:25.

rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟
rows.why: الهوا is singular masculine but he used the plural أجو; Amal questioned it twice and he said 'it's singular. Aja ktir'.
rows.english: The wind came a lot in the morning.

rows.medi_said: الهوا كـ كان قوي كتير الصباح
rows.why: 'In the morning' needs بـ / في (or الصبح alone); Amal said Nice. My reading.
rows.english: The wind was very strong in the morning.

rows.why: 'I cleaned it' needs the object ending; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said نظفتها.

rows.medi_said: Is it the bee? Is it the bee plants?
rows.why: He could not find 'plants' and asked; Amal supplied زريعة (sheet: plants (domestic) | Zri3a | زريعة).

rows.medi_said: I don't, أنا بعرف، ما بعرف.
rows.why: Amal asked for 'stones'; he said he did not know and she supplied حجر.
He meant the old streets in general (plural); Amal recast الشوارع and he repeated it.
rows.english: The old streets in America are stone.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. Made of is different than made.
rows.why: 'Made of stone' with مع (with) is wrong; Amal recast the sentence with just حجر ('الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر').
rows.english: The old streets in America are made of stone.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: 'The second stone' is تاني حجر or الحجر التاني; حجر تاني is 'another stone'. Amal recast and noted he said it right first.
rows.english: The second stone was my favorite.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Amal: المفضل is an adjective and never takes a pronoun ending; 'my favorite' alone is المفضل عندي.
rows.english: The second stone was my favorite.
rows.proposed_rule: An adjective like مفضل never takes a possessive ending; 'my favorite' on its own is المفضل عندي (or حجري المفضل).

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: The adjective goes after the noun; Amal named it ('المفضل is an adjective') and gave الحجر المفضل.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; Amal said 'No ال first' and he said حجري المفضل.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: For 'isn't here' he used في (there is); Amal recast مش هون and explained في means 'there is', and he took مش هون.
